negatives.statement: The first read-only lexical-audit helper used the Windows default console encoding and stopped when printing the word Māori after six candidate rows.
negatives.recovery: Rerun the same read-only audit with explicit UTF-8 output; all ten rows and the maximum score were then produced.

negatives.statement: The first privacy pattern set matched prohibition labels such as session streams and a phase-index tool name containing screenshot rather than concrete private payloads.
negatives.recovery: Refine the scanner to concrete identifiers, values, route schemes, local path values, credential forms, image payloads, transcript fields, and session-stream filenames; the full x1 packet then returned zero hits.

negatives.statement: The first staged-token review placed --cached after the grep pattern, so Git treated it as a revision and the pending-token subcheck failed.
negatives.recovery: Use git grep --cached before the pattern; the corrected rerun found exactly three permitted pending evidence tokens and zero sent-route tokens.

negatives.statement: The first closeout staged-name hash helper used System.Convert.ToHexString, which is unavailable in the host PowerShell/.NET surface, so the helper stopped after staging.
negatives.recovery: Keep the intact staging set and encode each SHA-256 byte with ToString('x2') before joining the hexadecimal receipt.

boundary: Runtime and validation failures are appended here and to the retained-negative register rather than erased after recovery.
